title: Route UID canonicalization must happen via RouteUID(), not inline
answers: Default routing tree RBAC permissions don't match between alias and canonical name
How is the routing tree UID computed from a name?
Provenance lookup fails for default route when using alias
Where does route name canonicalization happen now?
body:
Invariant: a ManagedRoute's UID must be produced by v1.RouteUID(name), which canonicalizes the default routing tree's legacy alias ('user-defined') to the same identity as its canonical name. This UID is NOT hashed like other ResourceUIDs — it is used verbatim as an RBAC scope suffix and a provenance-store key, so any change to the canonicalization logic breaks existing RBAC grants/provenance lookups for the default tree. ManagedRoute.GetUID() now just returns the stored UID string; it no longer re-canonicalizes r.Name, so construction sites (e.g. NewManagedRoute) are the only place canonicalization can occur.
Fix pattern/constraint: when constructing or converting a ManagedRoute (or comparing route identity, e.g. in service.go's imported-route lookups), always derive the UID via v1.RouteUID(name) / models.CanonicalizeRoutingTreeName(name) rather than assigning a raw name string.
applies: pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1 ManagedRoute and anything that constructs/compares its UID (pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/routes/service.go)

search: ManagedRoute UIDs must be canonicalized exclusively via v1.RouteUID(name) or models.CanonicalizeRoutingTreeName(name), never assigned inline; this UID is used verbatim as an RBAC scope suffix and provenance-store key, so any canonicalization logic change breaks existing RBAC grants and provenance lookups. The default routing tree's legacy alias 'user-defined' must map to the same identity as its canonical name through RouteUID. Applies to ManagedRoute construction sites (NewManagedRoute), imported-route lookups in service.go, and any comparison of route identity in pkg/services/ngalert/notifier.
